Read only this entrypoint and an explicitly supplied config/arguments first. Ask one compact round for missing answers:

1. Output: **new branch** (suggest `jev-convert/YYYY-MM-DD`), **clone to a new sibling/repo** (original untouched), or **report only** (no code changes)?
2. Access: **TypeSafe key**, **OpenRouter key**, **Vercel AI Gateway key**, or **neither**? Ask for the provider/env-variable name, never the secret in chat. Offer the hidden-input launcher in [credentials](references/credentials.md).
3. Risk: **conservative** (retain original fallback everywhere) or **aggressive** (Jev-only only where parity is proven)?

Use a structured question tool if available; otherwise ask in text and end the turn. Never infer an unanswered choice. Config or argument answers count; do not ask again. [Configuration](references/configuration.md) defines headless behavior, including missing answers.

After setup answers, run the read-only `scripts/preflight.py` with the answered mode/provider and relevant branch/path (see `--help`); inspect its JSON. `output.mode` alone chooses the mode: an inactive clone_path does not authorize cloning in branch/report mode. Check key **presence**, never its value; do not claim a key is absent without this check. A missing key permits approved code with validation skipped. Preflight verifies: git exists; repo status is clean (including untracked files); requested branch/path is unused. If dirty, offer stash or stop; do not stash without authorization. Do not create/switch branches, clone, install packages, write plans, or run source code during the audit. Keep git reads from refreshing the index (`GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`).

## 1. Audit — read-only

Read [audit rules](references/audit.md), the [official TypeSafe skill](references/official/typesafe-skill.md), current docs from its index, and applicable local repository guidance. Read API, Models, Confidence, building guide, coding-agents, Jev 1.13 jaggedness, the four Patterns pages, and relevant cookbooks before recommending integration. The official skill and its vendored references own API details; live docs win. Trace every LLM call and wrapper to all consumers. Inventory DECISION, GENERATION, MIXED, EXTRACTION and a reasoned fit verdict.

## 2. Recommend — present, then stop

Present a selectable table with original `file:line` IDs, classification, downstream use, fit, and 1–3 concrete options each. Each option states primitive, expected latency/cost direction **and why**, risk, and scope. Include leaving a site unchanged where appropriate. Generation is never Jev-only. With no suitable sites, say **"No good Jev opportunities here"** and explain why.

Wait for explicit option selections, edits, or acceptance. Do not write files until the answer. Explicit upfront approval can name sites/options or a precise predicate; resolve that predicate against the audit and show the resulting selections. Risk posture alone is not approval. Never expand approval to a MIXED site's generated part.

Read [conversion rules](references/conversion.md) and [validation](references/validation.md) before edits. After approval, establish the chosen output location and save `JEV_CONVERSION_PLAN.md` there with audit, options, selections and preflight facts. Write machine-readable `JEV_AUDIT.json` alongside it. In report mode write only report artifacts, never dependencies, env files, code, or git commits.

Keep all Jev questions, criteria, thresholds and a **versioned** model ID in **one decisions module per language**. Preserve signatures, return types, exceptions and observable diagnostics. Keep the original path for low confidence, malformed answers, errors, timeouts and rate limits; log answer path and model version without secrets/input contents. Use the real original path and actual converted decisions, not a new proxy prompt. Measure agreement, confidence curve, fallback rate, latency and cost; exercise forced failures. If no key, state **live validation skipped**, retain fallback, and never claim parity. A missing baseline key also prevents parity unless the user authorizes an equivalent provider route. A supplied authorization already answers that question. If preflight reports a key present, actually attempt the live checks; do not silently skip them or claim no key. Report transport failures accurately.

14	POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone

16	Content-Type: application/json
17	```

19	## Request body
20	
21	The top-level shape of every request. Each entry in the `questions` map is a typed question you name.
22	
23	<ParamField body="state" type="string | object | array" required>
24	  The content to evaluate. A plain string for text, or structured data (object/array) for things like chat logs, records, or the current state of your application. See [State](/concepts/state) for formats and best practices.
25	</ParamField>
26

29	</ParamField>
30

41	```json Example request theme={null}
42	{
43	  "state": "Help! My payouts have been failing for 3 days.",
44	  "model": "jev-latest",
45	  "questions": {
46	    "is_urgent": {
47	      "type": "noul",

55

57

62	  "potential_duplicate": {

74	
75	A yes/no question. Returns the probability the answer is yes.
76	
77	<ParamField body="type" type=""noul"" required />
78	
79	<ParamField body="instructions" type="string | object | array" required>

108	      }

124	<ParamField body="criteria" type="map<string, string | object | array | null>" required>

126	
127	  <Expandable title="map entries">
128	    <ParamField body="‹option›" type="string | object | array | null">

130	    </ParamField>
131	  </Expandable>
132	</ParamField>

134	```json Example request focus={5-13} theme={null}
135	{
136	  "state": "Help! My payouts have been failing for 3 days.",
137	  "model": "jev-latest",
138	  "questions": {
139	    "department": {
140	      "type": "choice",
141	      "instructions": "Which team should handle this?",
142	      "criteria": {
143	        "billing": "Payments, invoicing, refunds",
144	        "technical": "Bugs, outages, integrations",
145	        "sales": "Pricing, upgrades, new accounts"
146	      }
147	    }
148	  }
149	}
150	```

152	### Score
153	
154	Rates the state along a rubric you define. Returns a probability-weighted value across your levels.
155	
156	<ParamField body="type" type=""score"" required />
157	
158	<ParamField body="instructions" type="string | object | array" required>
159	  What the model should rate. An object can hold the question in one field and data it refers to in others; see [Use structure in the questions](/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one#use-structure-in-the-questions).

164	</ParamField>

169	  "model": "jev-latest",
170	  "questions": {
171	    "frustration": {
172	      "type": "score",

174	      "criteria": ["Calm", "Frustrated", "Very angry"]
175	    }
176	  }
177	}
178	```

181

185	  The model that performed the evaluation.

195	  </Expandable>
196	</ResponseField>

211	  "answers": {
212	    "is_urgent": {
213	      "type": "noul",
214	      "noul": 0.95
215	    }
216	  },
217	  "usage": { "input_tokens": 296, "output_tokens": 20 }
218	}
219	```

222	
223	Every answer carries a `type` matching its question. Choice and Score answers also carry a `confidence` between 0 to 1, derived from the answer's probability distribution. See [Confidence](/confidence).

226

252	</ResponseField>

255	  Every option mapped to its probability (floats that sum to 1).
256	
257	  <Expandable title="map entries">
258	    <ResponseField name="‹option›" type="number">

260	    </ResponseField>
261	  </Expandable>
262	</ResponseField>

265	  How certain the model is, derived from probabilities.
266	</ResponseField>

271	  "answers": {

274	      "choice": "billing",

276	      "confidence": 0.81
277	    }

280	}
281	```

284

286	
287	<ResponseField name="score" type="number" required>
288	  The probability-weighted answer across the levels; can land between levels.
289	</ResponseField>
290	
291	<ResponseField name="legend" type="map<string, string>" required>
292	  Each level number mapped back to its description.
293	</ResponseField>
294	
295	<ResponseField name="probabilities" type="map<string, number>" required>
296	  Each level (string key) mapped to its probability (floats that sum to 1).
297	
298	  <Expandable title="map entries">
299	    <ResponseField name="‹level›" type="number">
300	      A level index, as a string key matching legend.
301	    </ResponseField>
302	  </Expandable>
303	</ResponseField>
304	
305	<ResponseField name="confidence" type="number" required>
306	  How certain the model is, derived from probabilities.
307	</ResponseField>
308	
309	```json Example response focus={4-10} theme={null}
310	{
311	  "model": "jev-1.13.0",
312	  "answers": {
313	    "frustration": {
314	      "type": "score",
315	      "score": 1.05,
316	      "legend": { "0": "Calm", "1": "Frustrated", "2": "Very angry" },
317	      "probabilities": { "0": 0.0, "1": 0.95, "2": 0.05 },
318	      "confidence": 0.92
319	    }
320	  },

<ParamField body="criteria" type="map<string, string | object | array | null>" required>

  <Expandable title="map entries">
    <ParamField body="‹option›" type="string | object | array | null">

24	  state: { document: "I was charged twice. Please fix this ASAP." },
25	  questions: {

|--------|-----|----------------------|

| p95 | 571.6ms | 1360.7ms |

- Jev: $0.042/Mtok input, output free (source: TypeSafe docs, 2025)
- gpt-4o-mini: $0.15/Mtok input, $0.60/Mtok output (source: OpenAI pricing, 2025-07)
